criteria.A: A stages the complete target dataset in separate staging tables keyed by migration id, validates it there, then activates with one fenced batch that flips the installed-snapshot pointer and publishes staged rows; readers always resolve through the installed pointer.
criteria.B: B keeps installed and staged row versions side by side in the same tables, each variant tagged with its snapshot id; activation flips the installed-snapshot pointer so staged variants become visible, and superseded variants are retained or dropped per the plan directives.
criteria.C: C prepares target rows under a fresh model-namespace prefix in the same tables (copy-on-write per row) and activates by flipping a fenced per-model namespace alias; the old namespace is dropped after activation and readers resolve model names through the alias.

# Lane 03 S7 JEV context (verified, 2026-10-04)

## What lane 03 owns and has built (merged, main @ 160db71)

`@canlang/state` (`packages/state`) + `packages/contracts/src/state.ts`:
- `StoragePort` over three adapters: D1 (real `D1Database` API via miniflare
  locally), Durable-Object SQLite (`storage.sql`), and a test-only memory
  adapter. SQL tables: `records`, `receipts`, `history`, `outbox`,
  `schedules`, `unique_claims`, `fence_log`. 328/328 tests green incl.
  miniflare D1/DO legs.
- Fence: every `commit` asserts `expectedRevision` with a LEADING
  `fence_log(expected+1)` INSERT inside the same atomic batch; dense
  revisions, never reset. D1 `batch()` rolls back failed sequences, but a
  multi-batch rollout is NOT atomic. No cross-service / cross-team /
  cross-DO transactions are promised.
- Canonical invoke/admission with receipts, viewer policy projection,
  CRUD pipeline, outbox/schedule staging, transaction/read/system ports.
- Readers observe committed state only; results are deep copies with
  deterministic orderings.

## DESIGN §11 requirements the execution engine must satisfy

- `migration Owner from="snapshot-id"`: `from` must identify the EXACT
  compiler-produced installed owner snapshot. Missing/mismatched
  predecessor evidence BLOCKS the upgrade. Each old owner is retained,
  renamed once, or dropped; a target consumes at most one predecessor.
- Directives: `rename owner`, `drop owner`, `rename before.Model to
  Model`, `rename before.Model.field to Model.field`, `drop
  before.Model[.field]`, `backfill Model` (read-only `before` row +
  partially initialized desired `row`; no queries, no actor/clock/random,
  no effects), `invalidate before.handler`.
- Compilation produces a reviewable plan and performs NO data migration.
  Deployment closes admissions/writers/cleanup/dispatch, fences old
  runtimes, freezes predecessor input. Runtime prepares COMPLETE target
  state in RESUMABLE BOUNDED staging, records progress, VALIDATES it,
  then ACTIVATES it. Preparation failure leaves installed data selected.
- A logical package may span D1 + several DO authorities:
  preparation/activation is NOT a transaction across them. Partial
  activation keeps access closed; resume, never reopen old code on mixed
  layouts. No zero-downtime or automatic destructive rollback promised.
- `invalidate` reaches ONLY inventoried undispatched pending
  occurrences/intents carrying the PINNED predecessor async handler
  contract (name alone insufficient); records a skipped outcome, retains
  replay identity. In-flight / provider-accepted / uncertain deliveries
  need reconciliation; cannot be marked cancelled.
- History: actual stored-value conversion advances each affected row
  ONCE with trusted migration attribution; NAME-ONLY changes preserve
  row versions. Drops subject to locks/references/expiry/replay rules.
- SQLite schema-alteration restrictions inform generation; D1 tracks
  applied SQL migrations separately (provider-level, distinct from row
  evolution). DO class lifecycle config is distinct from row evolution.

## L7 framing (already landed in contracts/deployment.ts)

`UpgradePlan { from: OwnerSnapshotRef[], to: ArtifactIdentity,
pendingWork: PendingWorkDisposition[] }` and `UpgradeState` machine:
proposed -> admissions-closed -> staging -> staged -> activating ->
active (+ staging-failed / activation-failed / recovered-previous).
L7 orchestrates across owners; L3 executes PER-OWNER staging/validate/
activate calls within one authority at a time. L1 has NOT yet emitted a
compiled plan format; L3 defines the execution-side intake interim.

## Scale and bounds

Owner-local: one logical package / small app implicit package. Bounded
staging chunks with checkpoints (runtime-supplied bounded iteration).
Admissions are closed during staging/activation, so no user-write
contention; the fence still guards against stale runtimes and lost
updates between resume steps. Staged output must never become another
row's input; frozen `before` rows throughout.
